rows.name: Section 1.6.2, Theorem 1.4: B_n is residually finite and Hopfian (Magnus)
rows.reason: Residual finiteness and Hopfianity are separate Magnus consequences of the embedding B_n < Aut(F_n); no claim on this pair asserts or consumes them, and the page stops at the action, faithfulness and the word problem.

rows.name: Theorem 13, expressions (5) do not depend on the special braid-coordinate system
rows.reason: Artin's projection-coordinate expression (5) is an alternative encoding of a braid class; the scaffolded route identifies braid classes with mapping classes and their action on pi_1 instead, so no item consumes Theorem 13.

rows.name: Theorem 14, the groupoid of braid classes with end subsets of the X_i is isomorphic to the groupoid of substitutions
rows.reason: The pair proves faithfulness through the mapping-class action on the free group and the arc/Alexander straightening argument; Artin's groupoid isomorphism is an independent classical identification and is recorded here as a fallback, not consumed.

rows.name: Theorems 17-19 (normal form, center) on printed pp. 116-126
rows.reason: The normal form and center theorems belong to the later Garside page of the braid track, which proves them from its own sources; this pair consumes only the automorphism formulas and Theorems 15-16.

rows.name: Lemma2.9: unions of finite polygonal plane graphs admit a common finite subdivision
rows.reason: No independent graph-overlay theorem is needed for the single-arc extension; finite transverse representatives are handled in the existing general arc proof.

rows.name: Lemma2.10: outer-face preservation along a chain of overlapping polygonal plane graphs
rows.reason: This preliminary is used in the source arc-complement argument; this lane does not infer an arc neighborhood from connectivity and does not use the preliminary as an independent supplier.

rows.name: Theorem3.2: a closed plane set with at least three curve-accessible points has at most two complementary regions
rows.reason: The new local proof needs only Jordan curve separation, not the general closed-set bound.

rows.name: Theorem3.3: extending compatible homeomorphisms of 2-connected plane graphs (statement and proof opening on p.125)
rows.reason: The continuation was not read; no graph-extension theorem is invoked in the branched-double-cover arc proof.

rows.name: Section 4 proof remark: the two-complex argument is described as hand-waving and the normalization lambda=1 is declared unused
rows.reason: The sketch-level two-complex passage and the unused normalization lambda=1 are replaced on this page by the explicit equivariant cell model and the absolute differential computation, so no claim depends on them.

rows.name: Section 2.4, informal alternative proofs of the Basic Lemma described as convincing only to their author
rows.reason: The informal alternatives are not complete arguments; the scaffold uses the closed-compact-replacement existence proof together with the explicit absolute cellular model instead.

rows.name: Section 5, the (n-2,2) Temperley-Lieb representation as an image at t=-q^{-1}
rows.reason: The Temperley-Lieb specialization is a separate application of the same pairing machinery, not part of the linearity target, and no commissioned claim of this pair depends on it.

rows.name: Lemma 3.1, conjugation by T(q) interchanges (q,t) with (q^{-1},t^{-1})
rows.reason: The inversion lemma is an auxiliary symmetry of the algebraic model and is not used anywhere in the topological proof route scaffolded for this pair.

rows.name: Theorem 2.2, Garside/Thurston/Charney growth and normal-form properties of B_n
rows.reason: The normal-form lengths, rational-growth theorem and polynomial greedy-form algorithm are part of the independent algebraic route, unused by this commissioned topological LKB/faithfulness/linearity route. No assertion is made that every result of Theorem 2.2 is already published elsewhere in this library.

rows.name: Lemmas 4.1-4.5, chamber bases and the Garside-theoretic refinement of faithfulness
rows.reason: Krammer's chamber decomposition gives a second algebraic proof but is not required by the topological proof route; the scaffold records his Theorem 4.6 as the independent treatment.

rows.name: Proposition 3.6, H_2(F_n;Gamma_pi) is a free Z[H]-module of rank n(n-1)/2 with an explicit cellular basis
rows.reason: The cellular basis is an independent integral-freeness proof; adopting it as the commissioned closed-surface basis would require an explicit basis identification, which is recorded as an open comparison instead.
